Tech Report: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1058 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.
  • But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
  • It has been revealed that the smell of rotten food can make us recoil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.

But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

It has been revealed that the smell of rotten food can make us recoil. Certain sexual practices can provoke a similar reaction. And in today's polarized political climate, even political opponents can become objects of disgust.

According to recent reports, psychologists have long investigated whether sensitivity to disgust helps explain political beliefs. A review of 24 studies found that people who reported being more easily disgusted tended to hold more socially conservative views.

One explanation begins with evolution.

"We think that it evolved in part to reduce exposure to things that could make you sick," psychologist Yoel Inbar, of the University of British Columbia in Canada, told DW.

In a recent development, but disgust is not a single emotion. The Three-Domain Disgust Scale, developed in 2009, distinguishes three types:.

One theory is that people who are especially wary of germs and disease may also prefer traditional social rules.

Inbar explains that avoiding potential sources of infection can also mean missing out on latest experiences.

"Some people are more on the cautious conservative side, and some people are more on the exploring risk-taking side when it comes to pathogen exposure," he remarked.

Sources indicate that indeed, the language of contamination also appears in political rhetoric. During his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump repeatedly described immigrants as "poisoning the blood of our country." Trump has also described himself as a "germaphobe.".

Inbar acknowledges that the evidence linking sensitivity to disgust with conservative political beliefs remains uncertain.

In a recent development, "We have hypotheses. I don't know that we have as strong of evidence as I would like," Inbar mentioned.

Disgust is not exclusively conservative. And what people find revolting can depend on their values.

A 2020 study titled "Is Disgust a "Conservative" Emotion?" found that liberals and conservatives were disgusted by different things.

Conservatives, generally aligned with the Republicans in US politics, reported greater disgust at examples involving sexual behaviors and drug use, while liberals, generally aligned with the Democrats, reported greater disgust at animal abuse and environmental pollution.

However, when asked how easily disgusted they were in general, there was no clear difference across the political spectrum.

Some early studies suggested conservatives indicated stronger physical reactions to frightening or disgusting images, measured partly through changes in sweating.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But subsequent research, including a 2020 study by political psychologist Bert Bakker at the University of Amsterdam, struggled to reproduce those findings.

Studies based on questionnaires, however, have generally found that people with more conservative attitudes report being more easily disgusted.

"If bodily reactions don't differ across political groups, why do feelings?" Manos Tsakiris, of Royal Holloway and the Centre for the Politics of Feelings at the University of London, told DW.

Tsakiris and colleague Mariana von Mohr wondered whether the answer might lie in how people perceive and interpret signals from their bodies.

Scientists call the perception of internal sensations, such as hunger, breathing or a racing heart, "interoception." It's sometimes called our eighth sense, alongside the familiar five, plus our senses of balance and body position.

"A bodily signal doesn't arrive with a label attached," Tsakiris told DW. "We have to notice it and make sense of it.".

The researchers surveyed 632 US adults, asking how much they noticed and trusted signals from their bodies — a measure known as "interoceptive sensibility.".

They found that people who were more easily disgusted by sexual behavior tended to be more conservative, regardless of how aware they felt of their bodies.

But for moral disgust, the link to conservatism was found only among people who reported lower bodily awareness.

What particularly surprised Tsakiris was that perceived bodily awareness alone had no link to political views.

"People who are highly attuned to their bodies were neither more liberal nor more conservative," he noted.

Inbar questions whether all forms of disgust are equally useful for studying political attitudes.

He and Joshua Tybur, one of the creators of the Three-Domain Disgust Scale, generally prefer measuring pathogen disgust — reactions to potential sources of disease — rather than sexual disgust.

Questions about sexual disgust may already reflect conservative beliefs about sex.

"It's almost asking people the same thing twice," Inbar said.

The latest study found no significant link between pathogen disgust and conservative views.

Inbar wants the findings on bodily awareness and disgust tested again, with predictions set out in advance. For now, he considers them "suggestive at best.".

Tsakiris suggests that people who struggle to understand their bodily feelings may be more vulnerable to political messages telling them what those feelings mean.

"I know what you're feeling. You're feeling angry or you're feeling disgusted about this thing," he noted, illustrating how someone might put an emotional label on another person's unease.

Such labels could influence political behavior, he argues, although the study did not directly test this.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is how disgust can do political work: it can turn moral judgments about individuals into judgments about whole groups," he mentioned.

Industry observers note that the research cannot establish whether disgust shapes political beliefs or existing beliefs shape what people find disgusting. Bakker notes that political beliefs can influence how people describe their own personalities, suggesting the relationship could work both ways.

"Voting behavior is very complex and citizens make up their mind about politics in a complex way," he told DW.

Sources indicate that inbar also cautions against exaggerating disgust's importance. "The thing to emphasize in your story is that the relationship, while it's consistent, is quite small," he said.

"It's one of the many influences on people's politics.".

Tsakiris advocates what he calls "critical feeling": questioning our emotional responses to provocative material, including social media posts, just as we question the information itself.

He also emphasizes discussing our feelings with others and listening to different perspectives, even when we disagree.

Sources indicate that "Life and politics and democracy is a contact sport," he said. Edited by: Rosalie Delaney.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:25.

Ethan Nwaneri was the breakout star of Arsenal's 2024-25 season, but he has endured a difficult period for several months.

Short of game time at Arsenal, the 19-year-old Englishman was loaned to Marseille in the second half of last season. It was an underwhelming spell, during which the winger started only four times and was labelled a flop.

This season, Arsenal decided to send him out on loan again, this time to Borussia Dortmund.

Recent findings suggest that however, the England Under-21 international no longer really features in the intends of Niko Kovac. Although he was used on many occasions at the start of the season, Nwaneri has not been in Dortmund's starting line-up since 17 October, away to Union Berlin (0-0).

Since that game, he has made a string of appearances in the final minutes of matches and has been left on the bench for the big games, against Bayern Munich (2-2) and Arsenal (1-1).

As a result, the player, who belongs to Arsenal, has played only 29 minutes in the German club's last seven outings, which is insufficient game time. This situation could also benefit West Ham United.

According to FootballTransfers, West Ham are preparing a loan offer to bring Nwaneri to the club in January.

Sources indicate that the London club, 13th in the Championship, are looking to strengthen their squad in an attempt to return to the Premier League. However, the deal is far from straightforward, as Arsenal will first have to recall their youngster from Dortmund.

In a recent development, the British outlet points out that Nwaneri's loan at Borussia Dortmund does not include an option or obligation to buy. Arsenal have a recall clause which gives them the possibility of bringing their youngster back in January.

According to recent reports, however, the Bundesliga leaders paid a loan fee, reportedly between £3.4m and £4.3m (€4m-€5m), and are covering the player's wages. Therefore, if Arsenal activate the recall clause for Nwaneri, they would have to reimburse the loan fee to Borussia Dortmund.

It therefore remains to be seen whether Arsenal will be prepared to give up that compensation to allow their talented youngster to join an environment more conducive to his progress, and whether the London club will demand another paid loan this winter.

West Ham are, in any case, lurking and ready to position themselves for the deal.

Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that his best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor. He charmed children and adults alike with his iconic Tiger, Bear, Tiger-Duck and other animals.

Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.

It has been revealed that his best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines. The writer and illustrator died peacefully at the age of 95, his publisher Bernhard Feil confirmed on Wednesday.

Janosch was born as Horst Eckert on March 11, 1931, in Hindenburg (now Zabrze, Poland) in what was then Upper Silesia. After World War II, his family had to flee to Germany.

According to recent reports, in 1953, Janosch started studying at the Academy of Art in Munich, thinking that it would be easy to become an artist. He was however dismissed after just a few terms for "lack of talent.".

It has been revealed that but luckily for his later readers, Janosch did not give up. He continued to work as a freelance artist, soon discovering his second great gift, namely writing.

His first children's book about a horse named Valek was published in 1960.

Although Janosch became famous primarily for his children's books, he also wrote books for adults that focused on his own childhood.

Recent findings suggest that even though he wrote cheerful books for children, Janosch hardly had any positive memories of his own childhood, as his father was an alcoholic. He was beaten not only by him but also by his mother and grandmother. Raised in a strictly Catholic environment, he was continuously threatened to be punished by God.

Later on, Janosch tried to overcome the burden of his childhood memories by turning to alcohol as well.

Sources indicate that he always expressed a great deal of understanding for children, trying to encourage them to stand up for their rights. As a result of his childhood experiences, Janosch did not want to have children himself, and his attitude towards the Catholic Church always remained divided. "As I am a sinner and a heretic, God will let me live a long life so that I can return to the Church," he told his biographer Angela Bajorek.

Recent findings suggest that janosch's animal figures are endearing but not always well-behaved. They love all kinds of nonsense. But even if they lie to each other or put their own interests first, the true winner at the end of stories is always friendship and solidarity.

According to recent reports, janosch achieved his major breakthrough with "The Trip to Panama," a story about two friends, a little tiger and a bear, who set out to find their paradise in Panama. After touring around in circles, they finally end up where they started out; they realize that their journey was the destination. Janosch received the German Youth Book Prize in 1979 for the work.

Janosch's protagonists have become familiar to generations of children all over the world. They come up over and over again in the various stories carefully illustrated with water colors.

Sources indicate that there is the honest lion Hans from the toy chest who fails to catch a nutcracker with his lies. There is Schnuddel and a ridiculous bragger Günter the Box-Frog. And then there is a tiger that collects mushrooms while looking out for his devoted friend, a bear, who always stands up for him even when the tiger temporarily leaves him because of a little pig in one of the stories.

In a recent development, the "Tigerente," literally "Tiger-Duck," a wooden duck on wheels with yellow-brown stripes, appears on numerous pictures by the illustrator. At times, the animal has been tossed into a corner, at times it is hanging from the ceiling, or the Box-Frog pulls it across the drawing.

His iconic figures, especially the Tiger-Duck, have served as motifs on various items, from cups to stamps to jewelry, and even on airplanes. Film adaptations and TV series based on his stories were produced in German and English.

According to recent reports, guests who visited Janosch in Tenerife were impressed by his very modest lifestyle. He always noted that hanging around in his hammock doing nothing was what he enjoyed most. And yet Janosch remained very active until the end of his life.

According to recent reports, from 2013 to 2019, he wrote a column for the German weekly Die Zeit, taking on the role of Mr. Wondrak, who commented on world affairs. Shortly before his 90th birthday in 2021, the complete collection of his Mr. Wondrak columns were published as a book in German.

Sources indicate that like the protagonists in his stories, Janosch always tried to content himself with few things. As he wrote in one of his books: "He who needs almost nothing, has everything.".

This article was originally written in German.

Newcastle chiefs are inching closer to confirming a fresh stadium as their direction of travel.

We reported in last week’s Newcastle Confidential how advanced talks with Upcoming York investment bankers Goldman Sachs over financing the £1.3billion project had indicated significant progress on the decision to leave St James’ Park, with a 65,000-capacity stadium on nearby Leazes Park the intention.

Fellow Wall Street firm JP Morgan have now been appointed as advisers in selling a stake in the club, and this would be to inject new equity to help fund infrastructural developments, including a stadium.

Sources have stressed this is not a case of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund looking to sell the club, but rather by creating upcoming shares – potentially worth up to 25 per cent of the club – it raises capital for such a significant outlay.

According to recent reports, with Newcastle stated to be valued at £1.5billion, this could equate to a £375million cash injection. PIF would retain their majority ownership, even if diluted to around 63 per cent from its current 85 per cent holding.

As one source noted: ‘This is not about taking cash off the table, it is about funding growth.'.

Yasir Al-Rummayan and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund are not looking to sell Newcastle despite their prepares to sell a stake in the club.

It has been revealed that we understand Goldman Sachs are still involved, and their role will be to provide a loan or other investment to help finance the stadium. As we reported last week, the cost of a new home would not be exclusively funded by PIF and co-owner Jamie Reuben, with loans, share problems and investments all part of the package.

The expectation is that a upcoming stadium, rather than a St James’ renovation, will soon be recommended to the club’s owners by the executive team. It will then be up to PIF to sign off on the plans and for a public announcement to be prepared.

REVEALED: What Dedic was doing in bow and arrow fiasco!

Amar Dedic was firing arrows at a tree during his infamous countryside escapade, Confidential can now reveal.

The details of exactly what the Newcastle defender was doing with a bow and arrows in a Northumberland beauty spot can be shared for the first time after police closed the case, including the deployment of a helicopter to track him down.

The chopper was part of a major search operation in which Dedic and his friend were stopped by more than half a dozen patrol cars.

Investigators are now satisfied the 24-year-old posed no threat to the public after a 999 caller reported seeing two men walking by a reservoir with what they described as a ‘crossbow’. It was, in fact, a bow and arrows.

In a recent development, I can reveal that Dedic was not hunting animals (or the public) during his Harlow Hill adventure, but was instead using a tree for target practice. He and his pal were firing beyond a fence with the aim of landing their arrows in the trunk.

It has been revealed that however, while the recreational archers were walking back to Dedic’s car, the emergency call was made by a concerned member of the public. Police cars, including armed response, arrived on the scene but the Bosnian had left.

Amar Dedic was firing arrows at a tree during his infamous countryside escapade, which saw police despatch a helicopter to track him down.

Dedic has taken the misunderstanding in good spirits, and we can expect him to copy Harvey Barnes' archer celebration if he scores in the coming weeks.

This prompted controllers at Northumbria Police HQ to scramble a helicopter to join the hunt and, seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate, Dedic was pulled over amid a blaze of blue lights.

Adding to the incredulity of the situation was the sudden appearance of goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett, who helped Dedic and police during questioning. They were in the area by chance.

Dedic has taken the misunderstanding in good spirits and, if he does score his first goal for Newcastle in the coming weeks, we should expect a Harvey Barnes-style archer celebration.

Joelinton is set to return to action next week – in time for the Tyne-Wear derby.

It has been revealed that the 30-year-old started three league games after a previous injury absence before he broke down again, raising serious questions over his ability to withstand a Premier League season. Nonetheless, Joelinton’s involvement for the derby would be a major boost to Matthias Jaissle in his first taste of the fixture.

First images of Toon's luxury private members' club.

Newcastle have taken inspiration from NFL giants Dallas Cowboys as they explore intends for a luxury private members' club at their £190million training headquarters – and I can reveal stunning images of how the exclusive facility would look.

Confidential understands club chiefs have been studying some of the world's leading sporting complexes, including The Star, the Cowboys' spectacular training base in Texas, as they look to transform their own 260-acre site into a world-class destination.

And their ambitions could extend well beyond football. Newcastle have now approached existing hospitality clients and members of their business club to gauge interest in a private members' retreat within the proposed training complex at Woolsington, which is set to open in the summer of 2029.

We can reveal the first concept images of a private members' club at Newcastle's proposed £190m training base.

The Dallas Cowboys' HQ in Frisco, Texas is one source of inspiration for the envisaged facility at Woolsington (pictured).

The market research includes questions about whether prospective members would be interested in business meeting spaces, a licensed bar and leisure club facilities. The idea is to create an exclusive social and business hub alongside the fresh training ground, which will house the men's first team and academy, with further plans to integrate the women's team.

According to recent reports, the Dallas Cowboys' headquarters in Frisco, Texas, has provided one source of inspiration. Known as The Star, the sprawling development combines elite training facilities with hospitality, entertainment, restaurants and commercial spaces. Club officials have visited NFL facilities as part of extensive research into how the world's leading sports organisations operate away from matchdays.

The striking concept images that we are able to bring you offer a glimpse of the scale of Newcastle's ambition as they seek to build a complex that will rank as one of the best in world football.

Wilson's familiar new neighbour.

Sporting director Ross Wilson has a newly introduced neighbour – Matthias Jaissle!

The pair are now living in the same complex in the Jesmond area of Newcastle, after Jaissle spent an initial period staying in the Dakota Hotel on the city’s Quayside.

This should prove handy ahead of the January window, and the club’s transfer war room might well become Wilson’s living room!

The car park also offers a clue as to what time Jaissle is starting work every day, and given Wilson rarely sees the manager’s vehicle there in the morning, it is assumed he is at the club’s Benton base before the milkman!

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is out of the Dakota Hotel, having moved into the same complex as the club's sporting director Ross Wilson.

Finally, Newcastle have beaten Sunderland on Tyneside, 16 years after their last league victory!

Two teams of legends played a game of walking football at Newcastle’s Foundation building close to St James’ Park on Wednesday.

And we can reveal that Newcastle won 14-3! The Toon team included Shay Given, Olivier Bernard, Steve Howey, Shola Ameobi, Dummett, John Anderson and Kenny Wharton. The top scorers, surprisingly, were noted to be former left backs Bernard and Dummett!

The get-together was aimed at raising awareness over walking football opportunities, with the Newcastle Foundation and Sunderland’s Foundation of Light both supporting the sport through various initiatives.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that absent from the field since September 18 and the match against Union Berlin (7-0), Jamal Musiala made his return this weekend against Cologne (1-1), a match in which he played 20 minutes. Affected by a serious neurological health problem, the young 23-year-old German attacking midfielder is at the heart of a huge controversy across the Rhine. The reason? The management of Bayern Munich speaks (too) openly about the health concerns of its player, without really taking into account the traditional medical confidentiality so often respected in the world of football. Recently, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge even went a little further by discussing the financial aspect of the affair.

“What we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level he has so often displayed here. We need to talk to the family, the player and especially his representatives. These sums are no longer possible – sorry, with all due respect. » Words that shocked an entire country, as well as FIFPro. The international players’ union issued a statement ordering Bayern to respect their player. And if Bayern speaks this way about the Musiala case, it is because the German international (46 caps, 10 goals) has a contract until 2030 paid at the rate of €25 million gross per season. Suffice it to say that the Bavarian management fears more than ever having to pay so much every month for a player who could never again find his former level, even if it means causing an outcry.

Faced with the controversy, one of the bosses of Bayern, Jan-Christian Dreesen, spoke in the columns of Bild. “Everything has already been said about Musiala. We must now take care of him and let him play. I was delighted that he was on the field on Friday as planned. We now hope that it will return to its former form. The fans are concerned about this situation because each of our players is one of us. Jamal is one of us! This is precisely why we watch over him. So it was obvious that there would be a reaction. But to be honest, I was simply surprised by the reaction of FIFPro. This players association is not even represented in Germany »he confided, before continuing:.

Industry observers note that “I maintain my position: it is our duty to ensure that Jamal has time to recover and return to his former levels. At the same time, we also have a responsibility towards the club. Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge made the same comments, even if they phrased them differently. And I think that’s a very valid argument. (…) If I may say so, the discussion around our “Mia San Mia” (motto which notably advocates unity within the club, editor’s note) seems a little forced to me. No one noted we weren’t taking care of Jamal and doing everything we could to support him. But everything has already been said on the subject, and we should focus on taking care of him, instead of just talking. (…) Winter is just beginning and it will be long. I don’t think we should set a specific number of weeks for his return. We will assess the situation in a few months and take stock. Jamal’s situation is the same as any other player who has been out for two months. He needs time to come back. » Continued in the next episode.

Neto set for first Juventus game since 2017 and says his Turin chapter was still open

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (618 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Juvefc

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that norberto Neto is set for his first competitive game in almost six months when Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League on Thursday night.
  • According to recent reports, neto last played for Juventus in May 2017, when he was part of the side that beat Lazio 2-0 in the Coppa Italia final.
  • His most recent competitive outing came on 30 May with Botafogo, as Football Italia noted after Wednesday’s press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that norberto Neto is set for his first competitive game in almost six months when Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League on Thursday night. Speaking on the eve of the match, the 37 year old goalkeeper said he still felt he had unfinished business in Turin.

According to recent reports, neto last played for Juventus in May 2017, when he was part of the side that beat Lazio 2-0 in the Coppa Italia final. More than nine years on, the Brazilian is in line to start again in black and white, with first choice Guglielmo Vicario being rested for the visit of the Cypriot side to the Allianz Stadium.

His most recent competitive outing came on 30 May with Botafogo, as Football Italia noted after Wednesday’s press conference. Since then he has been working as cover, a role he took on after joining as a free agent at the end of September.

It has been revealed that juventus moved for Neto after Kamil Grabara ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in training on 19 September, only days after keeping a clean sheet on his debut against NEC. The club confirmed his return on 28 September with a contract running until 30 June 2027.

In a recent development, asked what drew him back, Neto explained that he had been looking for a next step that genuinely meant something to him. “Deep down, I felt my chapter with Juve was still open,” he said, in comments reported by ilBianconero, which carried the press conference live. He added that he is enjoying his work and is in Turin to help, whatever the coming months bring.

Opening the press conference, he described his feelings simply: “It’s hugely satisfying. I’m really excited to be back on the pitch, and proud to be part of this team.”.

In a recent development, neto was asked about Vicario, who is on loan from Tottenham and has been Luciano Spalletti’s regular choice in goal. He kept his answer short: “I don’t know how much my opinion matters, but he’s a top-level goalkeeper.”.

Sources indicate that the veteran also spoke warmly about the younger players around him. He noted their eagerness to contribute was infectious and that the squad has the quality, will and determination it needs. On the goals Juventus have conceded this season, he pointed to a side that is still developing, with several players newly introduced to Serie A and finding their way. His own focus, he said, is on training at full intensity every day while the team looks for balance and consistency.

Juventus go into matchday five fifth in the league phase standings with ten points from four games. Omonia have won two and lost two. Neto warned against taking them lightly, saying they are a strong side who break forward with real quality, and revealed he knows their coach Fabiano from his years in Brazil.

He also stressed that Europe brings its own demands, noting that Juventus always carry a responsibility to compete to win in every tournament they enter.

Interest in the meeting was already strong after ticket sales for Omonia passed 35,000 last week. Next up in Serie A is the trip to Como, where both sides go in without suspensions.

For Neto, the night is a chance to add to the 22 appearances he made in his first spell, when he won two league titles, two Coppa Italia trophies and a Supercoppa Italiana as Gianluigi Buffon’s understudy.

#140464. Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains

Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4361 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot–superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man’s Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron–hole character, but lack topological protection3,4,5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man’s Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6,7,8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man’s Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains.

According to recent reports, wiring diagram for the DC and RF lines used to measure the device, with properties and components detailed in the legend. Additional details can be found in ‘Measurement set-up’ in Methods.

According to recent reports, a, Detailed schematic of the pulse sequence, showing the various stages of the protocol. b, p(ee∣ee), p(oo∣ee), p(ee∣oo), and p(oo∣oo) as a function of pulse duration and pulse ramp time. Parity oscillations remain visible even for slow ramp duration up to approximately 75 ns. An oscillation as a function of ramp duration is also visible at zero pulse duration, indicating that the qubit evolves partially during the ramp of the coupling pulse. c, Time trace and corresponding histogram of the readout signal \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) with the left chain on resonance and the right-chain QDs off-resonance, using 400 μs readout time. Transitions between \(| e\rangle \) and \(| o\rangle \) are attributed to quasiparticle poisoning. d, Dwell time histogram from c. e, p(e∣e), p(o∣e), p(e∣o), and p(o∣o) while varying the pulse amplitude VC and ramp time. For fast ramps (≲5 ns), parity mixing is observed between the chain and the dot. We attribute this to a diabatic excitation of the coupled system, which rapidly decoheres before the final measurement. In the main text, we use ramp times of 25 ns to avoid these excitations. For pulse amplitudes ≲11.5 mV, no parity mixing is observed, which we use to roughly identify when QDC passes through resonance. f, Schematic of the configuration for the measurements in c-e. g-j, Same as c-f, but for the right chain, with the QDs of the left chain off-resonance. In panel i, parity mixing between the chain and QDC is observed for ramp times  ≲ 10 ns, indicating a slightly weaker coupling between QDC and the right chain versus the left chain.

In a recent development, readout characterization using time traces of the reflected resonator signal \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\), measured for three different amounts of detuning with the coupler QD kept fixed far from resonance. Thresholds used for single-shot state identification are obtained by fitting a Gaussian mixture model. The detuning configuration in (e-g) is used for qubit readout. a, Schematic representation of the readout configuration with both chains on resonance. b, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in a. Residual coupling between the chains results in inter-chain hopping that is faster than the readout time of 500 μs, preventing readout in a single shot. The two quantum capacitance signals corresponding to the \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) states are partially averaged which makes them difficult to distinguish from the \(| oe\rangle \) and \(| eo\rangle \) states. c, As in a, but with both chains detuned from resonance. d, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in c. The slight detuning suppresses inter-chain hopping, though it remains too fast for high-fidelity single-shot readout. Two distinctive regions can be observed: When the system is in the global even state, rapid jumps between \(| oo\rangle \) and \(| ee\rangle \) are visible. When the system is poisoned, it enters the global odd manifold. Transitions between \(| oe\rangle \) and \(| eo\rangle \) are not resolved because they produce similar readout signals. e, As in c but with both chains detuned further from resonance. f, Time trace of \(\Delta {S}_{{\rm{M}}}^{{\rm{11}}}\) and corresponding histogram for the readout configuration in e. The two computational states \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) correspond to the red and blue signals, and can now clearly be resolved. The green signal contains both leakage states of the odd global parity manifold (\(| eo\rangle \) and \(| oe\rangle \)). Due to the antisymmetric detuning where the ground state of one dot is full and the other is empty, the \(| oo\rangle \) state is energetically favored over the \(| ee\rangle \) state, resulting in a skewed population between the two. Transitions are mainly observed between the even and odd global manifolds. The signal-to-noise ratios between the leakage distribution and the \(| ee\rangle \) and \(| oo\rangle \) distributions are 2.88 ± 0.28 and 2.76 ± 0.09, respectively. Integrating the fitted Gaussian distributions across the assignment thresholds gives false-leakage probabilities of 0.45% for \(| ee\rangle \) and 0.25% for \(| oo\rangle \), showing that finite readout SNR accounts for only a small fraction of the observed leakage. g, Dwell time histogram of the three observed states, indicating the difference in lifetimes. The shortest measured state lifetime in this readout configuration is 8.3 ms, corresponding to a probability of approximately 5.8% for a state transition during the 500 μs integration window. The trace is acquired with the coupler QD kept far from resonance, showing that state switching on this timescale is already present in the readout configuration. These transitions include both residual inter-chain hopping and quasiparticle-poisoning events and can produce time-averaged signals that are assigned as leakage for pulsed measurements.

Recent findings suggest that conditional probabilities at the simultaneous sweet spot for the two chains in both the even and odd global parity manifolds, corresponding to Extended Data Fig. 5g but extended to larger pulse amplitudes. Additional outer lines appear when the energy of the detuned chain is aligned with the first excited state of the other chain. The quadrant in which they appear depends on the initial state of the system, as well as the global parity manifold (‘Interpretation of pulsed charge-stability diagrams’ in Methods). a, Left chain in the even manifold. b, Right chain in the even manifold. c, Left chain in the odd manifold. d, Right chain in the odd manifold. The QDR2 resonance is shifted by approximately 3 mV with respect to panel b due to the Coulomb interaction with the additional electron on the parity-switching QD. The odd-manifold measurements include two parity-switch passages, before and after the control sequence. Comparing the background return probabilities in the even- and odd-manifold measurements for initial states \(| oo\rangle \) and \(| oe\rangle \) gives single-passage parity-switch fidelity of 99.77 ± 0.03% (‘Parity-switch fidelity’ in Methods).

a, Map of p(oo∣oo) (left) and p(oe∣oe) (right) as a function of the left and right hybrid-gate voltages (VLH and VRH). The diagonal and antidiagonal features of enhanced parity mixing correspond to degeneracies between the qubit basis states. The points labeled c-k indicate the VLH,VRH values used in the remaining panels. b, Schematic representation of the four configurations measured at each point: left- and right-chain pulsed charge-stability diagrams in the global even and odd parity manifolds. c-k, Pulsed charge-stability diagrams measured for the left and right chains in the even (top) and odd (bottom) parity manifolds. Unlike conventional charge-stability diagrams referenced to the Fermi energy in a normal lead, here each chain provides the energy reference for the other. As such, the measured features reflect the difference between the excitation energies of the two individual chains. Crossings are therefore observed simultaneously for the left and right chains when the splittings of the two chains compensate each other, corresponding to the qubit degeneracy condition. Consequently, the appearance of a crossing in a single parity manifold does not imply that the corresponding chain is tuned to its sweet spot. Indeed, crossing-like features are observed in only one manifold in panels c, e, i and k. The orientation of the avoided crossings depends on the parity manifold: in the even manifold, the left and right chains exhibit the same orientation, whereas in the odd manifold the orientation is reversed, reflecting the sign difference ε12 ± ε34 between the two manifolds. Only near the sweet spot (panel g) are crossings observed for both chains in both parity manifolds simultaneously, providing a unique signature that both chains are individually tuned to their sweet spots.

The value of VC is indicated above each panel. The device configuration is the same as in Extended Data Fig. 8. a-h, The superconducting phase difference between the chains is set to φ ≈ 0. As VC is made more negative, the coupler QD is first brought closer to resonance and parity mixing along the degeneracy lines increases. Eventually, when the coupler QD is near or below resonance (around VC = − 9 mV), the final state is dictated by the ground state of the chain in the relevant sector of the charge-stability diagram irrespective of the initial state. We note that the chain appears to move from CAR-like at low pulse amplitudes (tR < ΔR, a) across a sweet spot (tR ≈ ΔR, b-e) to ECT-like at high pulse amplitudes (tR > ΔR, f-h), which we attribute to uncompensated cross-capacitance between VC and VRH. i-n, The superconducting phase difference between the chains is set to φ ≈ π. The main difference is that the visibility of QDR2 is suppressed, as predicted by theory (Supplementary Note 4).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the winter transfer window should be rather calm on the Castellana side. After a somewhat sluggish start to the season, which earned early criticism from Mourinho and a good number of players in the squad, the Merengues found their cruising speed and caught up with Barça in La Liga, in addition to achieving a perfect run in the Champions League. Everything seems to be going well, and, a priori, no need to strengthen this winter.

The Merengue leaders are not very fond of winter recruitment in any case. On the other hand, in terms of departures, there could be movement, with players who could leave on loan, like the young Thiago Pitarch, barred by competition in midfield. But if there’s one name that’s going to be talked about in January, it’s Endrick. It is difficult, at present, to know the player’s prepares. What is certain is that he does not seem to totally matter to José Mourinho, who has only started him once this season (for 8 TCC appearances in total).

Recent findings suggest that A difficult situation for a player who needs playing time to continue his progress. Especially since there is no shortage of suitors, with a good number of Premier League and Serie A clubs dreaming of welcoming him. It is AC Milan which seems the hottest on the file, and the Cadena SER has just confirmed the interest of the Lombards in the 20-year-old striker. Better, the media indicates that an offer of 70 million euros has already been made, and that it has therefore already arrived on the desk of the management of Real Madrid. AC Milan have even already spoken with Endrick to express their interest.

For the moment, José Mourinho does not wish to part ways with the player. For his part, Endrick is not necessarily leaning towards leaving but the former Palmeiras’ entourage could push him to pack his bags. In the event that a transfer is not possible this winter, the Milanese team has already planned to go on the attack again this summer. A sign that Ruben Amorim and the Milanese decision-makers are really counting on him. On the Merengue side, we would even make a small added value on the player, who had cost 35 million euros fixed + 25 million euros in the form of bonuses which have not yet been reached. To be continued….

  • He is a bit annoying, but he strikes the ball and drives it with both feet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:53.

Rayan Cherki made a strong impression on Jeffinho during their time together at Olympique Lyonnais in 2023. Appearing as a guest on the Charla Podcast, the Brazilian forward first praised the technical qualities of the current Manchester City player, before describing a much more divisive character.

'Rayan Cherki. What a player! He is a bit annoying, but he strikes the ball and drives it with both feet. He is very strong' - he explained.

Jeffinho then went on to explain what could bother him about the Frenchman. 'You can see it in the way he plays. He dribbles and looks at the others' - the Brazilian mentioned, naming Bradley Barcola among the best players he has played alongside and liked.

The testimony becomes even more interesting when he discusses relationships within the Lyon dressing room.

According to Jeffinho, Cherki belonged to a fairly closed group that also included Corentin Tolisso, Alexandre Lacazette and Anthony Lopes. The Brazilian describes a 'small clique' of important players who stayed together a lot and, in his view, had real influence in the team.

At the time, Lyon's management had nevertheless denied the existence of a 'Lyonnais gang'.

Asked about the player with the most assertive temperament in this circle, Jeffinho naturally named Cherki.

He explained that the group 'weighed a little on the team', while not hiding that their attitude could sometimes annoy him. His testimony remains nuanced, however: with each criticism of the Frenchman's behaviour, the former Lyon player returns to his immense quality as a player.

Recent findings suggest that jeffinho also extended his judgement to Cherki's current situation at Manchester City. 'Cherki plays extremely well, but you also have to respect the others' - he remarked, before suggesting that his attitude could sometimes have a negative impact on his team.

A very personal view of the attacking midfielder, but one that above all sheds light on the relationships he observed in the Lyon dressing room.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that roma came from behind to draw 2-2 with holders Paris Saint-Germain, with substitute Donyell Malen scoring a 78th-minute penalty. The leaders' rivals above Juventus showed the depth of their squad less than a month before they host Spalletti's side.

In a recent development, roma left the Parc des Princes with a point and with their reputation enhanced. Mario Hermoso gave them the lead against the European champions. Paris Saint-Germain turned the game around through an Illia Zabarnyi header and an Ousmane Dembélé penalty.

In Europe, Malen’s spot-kick was his fifth goal. Across all competitions, it marked his 17th strike of the campaign, from 16 appearances. It came days after he scored four times in Roma’s 5-1 win at Parma. Yet he did not start in Paris, and neither did Paulo Dybala. Gian Piero Gasperini mentioned he left Malen out because of the number of games he had played for Roma and the Netherlands.

Industry observers note that that a reshuffled Roma could take a point in Paris says plenty about their squad. Luis Enrique’s side had not dropped points since a home defeat to Monaco on 4 September.

The result does not fix Roma’s European position. The club lists the game as Matchday 5 of the league phase. Roma have one win, two draws and two defeats so far. Under the format, clubs finishing 9th to 24th enter the play-offs, while 25th to 36th are knocked out. The top eight go straight into the round of 16.

It has been revealed that that leaves Roma with work to do in a crowded December. Their next Champions League match is at home to Sporting CP on 8 December, kicking off at 21:00. They then travel to AEK Athens on 19 January and host Lille on 27 January 2027.

Industry observers note that domestically, Roma’s form has been strong. Their league record shows nine wins and three draws, with 36 goals scored and 11 conceded, Corriere dello Sport reported.

For Spalletti’s side, the schedule offers some contrast. After that European fixture, Roma play the derby away to Lazio on Sunday 13 December at 12:30. That leaves them six days between the derby and the visit of Juventus. Before travelling to Rome, Juventus are away to Como on 29 November. Udinese and Monza then come to Turin in Serie A, on 6 December and 14 December respectively.

In a recent development, whether Roma’s European commitments take a toll remains to be seen. The evidence from Paris suggests Gasperini can rotate without a sharp drop in quality. Malen’s form, from the bench or from the start, will be a central concern for Juventus.

The two sides meet in round 16 of Serie A on Saturday 19 December 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.

#140460. Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head

📅 24 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 22m • 📚 Deep Dive (4480 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Sensational Spurs storm Stamford Bridge as Palmer loses his head

📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4480 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players.
  • This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.
  • Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V.

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

Sources indicate that jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had said he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

According to recent reports, in between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

Spurs have taken the lead after Mateus Fernandes' corner ends up in Chelsea's goal ⚽️ https://t.co/X65gyO9yPX.

A man and a goal down, Chelsea then saw hundreds of their own fans walk out when Mathys Tel scored a brilliant second for Spurs with three minutes remaining. The visiting fans, who had seen one win at the Bridge since 1990 prior to Saturday, could hardly believe what they had seen.

"Just look what it means!" A glorious solo run and finish from Mathys Tel! 🤩 https://t.co/Qg7WMFNlwQ.

Industry observers note that tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. The two benches had clashed and De Zerbi had been booked after Palmer’s first yellow card that the Italian felt should have been a red. But De Zerbi will not care about that now, with Tottenham’s season finally up and running thanks to successive league wins against Coventry City and Chelsea.

"They were brilliant Spurs, they really were" Gary Neville's immediate reaction to Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham 🗣️ https://t.co/QWhi7Blmfz.

Sources indicate that tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

With Solanke resting up on the bench until the 65th minute, De Zerbi moved Omar Marmoush, who had scored his first Spurs goal against Coventry, into the middle and brought in Tel on the left.

Tel was involved in the 29th-minute move that should have resulted in the opening goal for Marmoush. The Frenchman played a one-two with Andy Robertson and the Scotsman picked out Marmoush with a low cross. But, six yards out and with time to pick his spot, the former Manchester City man allowed Penders to make a save.

Industry observers note that the missed Marmoush chance was the first time Penders had been called into action. At the other end, Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky made unnecessary work for himself.

Recent findings suggest that kinsky played a bad pass straight to Pedro Neto. The ball was worked to Henderson, but Kinsky recovered to make a save and then stopped the follow-up from Neto. The offside flag then went up, but it was unclear whether it would have spared Kinsky on both occasions had Chelsea scored.

It was not the first time Kinsky had handed possession back to Chelsea in a dangerous area, although the 23-year-old had also made a good save to palm away a curling effort from Palmer. That came after Fernandes had the ball pinched from him far too easily.

Neto was Chelsea’s most dangerous player, but it was the wrong call by Alonso to leave Danny Welbeck on the bench, with João Pedro out injured, and he was too slow to change things. Leaving it until the 88th minute, when the game had already been killed by Tel, to send on the striker was a clear error.

Storm Boelo created wet-and-wild conditions on the Stamford Bridge pitch, while there were still remnants of Storm Austen, or should that be Storm Austin, on the home bench.

Chelsea set-piece coach Austin MacPhee let out an incredibly loud “for f---’s sake” when one corner routine went wrong. Nobody could hear what he was shouting over the Tottenham celebrations when Penders scored his own goal, but it would almost certainly have started with “f” again.

James Maddison had been a doubt before the game after missing training during the week and it only took four minutes of the second half for him to signal to De Zerbi that he needed to come off.

Maddison had scored a brilliant goal on his first league start in 18 months against Coventry, but he had to be replaced by former Chelsea midfielder Gallagher at Stamford Bridge.

James Maddison is forced off with an injury and is replaced by Conor Gallagher, who receives a mixed reception from his former fans 🔃 https://t.co/GSeXQQ3eoa.

The Chelsea fans predictably booed Gallagher, a graduate of the club’s academy who at times even stood in as captain. The foul on Gallagher that earned Palmer his marching orders silenced the jeers and the Chelsea fans’ boos only returned at the final whistle for their own players.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

In a recent development, “I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso stated. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”.

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”.

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

According to recent reports, but Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He noted: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”.

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

“We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi said. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”.

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

Sources indicate that “We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso stated. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”.

A long-awaited Stamford Bridge victory for @SpursOfficial 👏 https://t.co/Qqwgbuj3Y3.

“When we have dinner together and spend time together in the dressing room, I see a different group, different relationships and a different atmosphere among the players.

“The character was great today, but we have many, many new players. The players who stayed here from last season and two or three seasons ago suffered from the results, including two 17th-place finishes.

“We are working to change the last part of the club’s history. We are lucky because we have many great people in the dressing room and many great players. I think if we work hard, we can do something key.

“The week in Marbella, speaking face to face, opening ourselves up and removing the mask, was notable for the spirit and belief.

“The atmosphere inside the dressing room is maybe more key than the tactics.”.

According to recent reports, speaking to Sky Sports, the Tottenham boss said: “It was a significant moment for the fans, the club and the players. They deserved this win and prepared very well.

Sources indicate that “We are improving a lot in our mentality, as a group and in our relationships with the players. We are also improving on the pitch.

Sources indicate that “Against Aston Villa and Everton, for 30 minutes we were playing very well. Maybe we didn’t score because our finishing wasn’t good enough, and perhaps in the first difficult moment we changed our mentality.

Sources indicate that “Now we are a complete team. The players are playing better and we have improved our style.

“I have to believe in this group. I never lost confidence in my players.

BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount

💡 Key Takeaways
  • German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.
  • Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW said.
  • The main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.

Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW said.

The main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China. Although the organization sold more cars in the US and Europe compared to the same period last year, this could only partially offset the decline in China.

BMW's car deliveries in China, which were already at their lowest level since 2017 last year, fell 24.8% in the quarter and consequently dragged global deliveries down by 6.3.

CEO Milan Nedeljkovic said his manufacturer would "specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

BMW on Tuesday also lowered its outlook for the current year, citing the faster-than-planned implementation of restructuring measures that includes 8,000 layoffs in its home market.

German carmakers have been struggling to compete with their Chinese counterparts in the electric vehicle market,  resulting in cost-cutting measures.

Volkswagen, the world's second-largest carmaker, is battling mounting competition from falling demand in its core Chinese market.

BMW, and its industry heavyweight peers, Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, have announced prepares to scale back production and reduce costs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Volkswagen Group posted its worst quarterly results in more than a decade earlier this October.

Industry observers note that it is looking to cut about 15% of its workforce worldwide, or 100,000 jobs, by the end of the decade. BMW has declared that it will cut up to 8,000 jobs — about 5% of its workforce — by the end of 2027.

On the other hand, German auto parts supplier Schaeffler declared on Tuesday that it planned to cut almost 3,500 jobs and close five sites in Europe, by 2028.

According to the manufacturer statement, three-fourths of the 3,460 job cuts and four of the five site closures will be in Germany.

German automotive supplier Bosch, the world's biggest, announced last year that it would cut 13,000 jobs, mostly in its auto division.

Chelsea Confidential: Meet Sebas Parrilla, the fiery, marathon-running, Bruce Springsteen fan Xabi Alonso trusts above all others - and why he's the man to fix Blues' defensive crisis

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1621 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • Xabi Alonso is not alone in trying to halt Chelsea’s lurch into crisis.
  • There is Willie Isa, the ‘cultural architect’ preparing the defenders for headed duels by acting as a human shield in training drills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 25 November 2026.

Xabi Alonso is not alone in trying to halt Chelsea’s lurch into crisis. He is surrounded by a small army of staff. Some may be familiar to you, others less so.

There is Willie Isa, the ‘cultural architect’ preparing the defenders for headed duels by acting as a human shield in training drills.

There is Andre Reis, the new set-piece analyst studying Nottingham Forest’s approach to corners so Austin MacPhee can formulate instructions for the team.

Industry observers note that there is Simon Morris and Stu Sullivan, the sports massage therapists preparing the players for their Friday night turnaround. And so on.

But the voice Alonso trusts most at Chelsea belongs to Sebastian Parrilla Simione, better known as ‘Sebas’.

The little-known Argentinian, a 49-year-old with a UEFA Pro Licence and love of marathon running and Bruce Springsteen, is his closest confidant and has been by his side ever since they oversaw an unbeaten season for Real Madrid’s Under 14s in 2018-19.

Xabi Alonso's most trusted lieutenant is Sebastian 'Sebas' Parrilla, a 49-year-old Bruce Springsteen fan with a tendency to get fired up on the touchline.

According to recent reports, alonso had asked for an experienced aide to assist him at Real, and he was handed Parrilla, who was born in Argentina, raised in Spain, and despite not playing professionally had worked for Madrid’s academy since 2002. Parrilla coached all age ranges, from the Under 11s to the B team.

Recent findings suggest that he had Alonso’s ear as their Under 14s won all but one game, and their bond was strong enough that Parrilla ended his 17-year association with Madrid’s academy when he accompanied his manager to Real Sociedad B in 2019. Then he followed him to Bayer Leverkusen in 2022, back to Real Madrid in 2025, and now Chelsea.

There is a little fire to Parrilla. He is already one caution away from a touchline suspension, having been booked against Tottenham Hotspur and Everton. While the analytical Parrilla prefers a low profile, he is Alonso’s alter ego.

The English winter will not only test Parrilla’s preference for wearing shorts whatever the weather, but also Chelsea's ability to arrest their slump with games coming thick and fast – there are seven Premier League fixtures to tackle between now and 2027, starting with Forest on Friday.

One area of focus on the training field this week has been defence. Chelsea have conceded 20 goals in the Premier League, as many as they have scored. Their shakiness at the back has been their downfall of late, and Parrilla was credited with helping organise the Leverkusen back line which went unbeaten in winning the Bundesliga in 2023-24.

When Leverkusen won 5-1 away at Eintracht Frankfurt in May 2024 to maintain their Invincibles tag with two games to go, Alonso was serving a touchline ban. Parrilla manned the technical area and after full time, Granit Xhaka and Co celebrated by pouring water over him.

Parrilla was fine with that, but less pleased during the game with how they conceded a goal from a corner to Hugo Ekitike and gifted other chances to Omar Marmoush.

One source at Leverkusen that we consulted this week credited Parrilla with improving players individually and taking the lead on set-pieces.

When Leverkusen scored from one corner routine against Hoffenheim in November 2023, Parrilla was the architect. He had certain players act as barriers to stop defenders from rushing to block the ball as it was rolled to the edge of the box, where Alex Grimaldo was on hand to power home.

Chelsea have their own set-piece specialist in MacPhee, poached from Aston Villa in the summer, so Parrilla has less control over set-pieces at Cobham.

It has been revealed that we do not yet know whether Alonso and Parrilla will decide to change Chelsea’s centre backs for Forest. Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana were bullied by Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey and Leeds United’s Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the last two losses.

Former Chelsea man Liam Delap is the next No9 to contend with, and won't be short on motivation.

There is the added complication that Fofana has conducted an unauthorised interview, released this week, in which he laughed off Chelsea's Carabao Cup exit after his penalty miss at Liverpool. Chelsea declined to comment when asked whether that would lead to any internal punishment.

Alonso and Parrilla have been joined at the hip since the former began working with Real Madrid's Under 14s in 2018.

Levi Colwill was bullied by Leeds' Dominic Calvert-Lewin in Chelsea's humiliating 4-1 loss last weekend.

Recent findings suggest that alonso’s options are limited. Frustrated as he will have been by his side's 4-1 loss to Leeds, he had no senior replacements for Colwill or Fofana to call on from the bench. The only substitute with 'experience' at centre back was 18-year-old Olutayo Subuloye.

Aaron Anselmino, who represented Argentina in the last international break but has not appeared for Chelsea at all this season, did not make the matchday squad.

It has been revealed that maxence Lacroix is still sidelined, but Alonso told us last week he hopes he will return before 2027. Josh Acheampong and Jorrel Hato could be used centrally rather than as full backs.

As well as assisting Alonso, Parrilla acted as a bridge to the academy at Leverkusen, regularly in contact with Sergi Runge when he was head coach of the Under 17s and Under 19s.

Despite the success of the first team, Parrilla never lost the love for coaching youngsters, agreeing to help the Under 8s with community sessions on occasion. Throwing in Subuloye, who was on Chelsea’s pre-season tour in the summer but has yet to appear competitively, would surely be too massive of an ask.

Until better options arrive, it would seem Parrilla is having to try to work his magic in the shadows with Colwill and Fofana. Both players know they need to improve – and fast.

Chelsea have headaches on the horizon, with Alejandro Garnacho not their only loan star struggling to convince his new club of his worth.

In a recent development, garnacho suffered the ultimate indignity when Aston Villa lost 1-0 to Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday. Despite Unai Emery being able to name 12 substitutes in Istanbul, he took only 11 with him including two goalkeepers, and still excluded Garnacho. When asked why, Emery said: ‘The players who were here are who I think are the best players to be here with us.’.

According to recent reports, garnacho, 22, joined Villa on a season-long loan with a £42.5million conditional obligation dependent upon making a certain number of appearances. It is still not being disclosed how many matches it would take to trigger the clause, which has been described by sources as confidential. Chelsea insiders previously claimed it was easily achievable.

Alejandro Garnacho (right) is one of several Chelsea players having a miserable time out on loan.

In a recent development, but Garnacho has appeared only four times in the Premier League this season, and the last of those appearances was a three-minute cameo against Fulham on October 31. He has not yet started a game in any competition.

While there is no break clause in the contract, it is understood it is possible for both Villa and Chelsea to agree to terminate his loan in January. That situation is one to watch.

But Garnacho is not the only problem loanee that Chelsea might need to address in the near future.

Robert Sanchez is on a 'dry' loan at Como, meaning there is no option or obligation to buy. The 29-year-old Spaniard has started just five of 17 games in all competitions this season.

In a recent development, another goalkeeper, 24-year-old Filip Jorgensen, is on loan at Chelsea’s sister side Strasbourg, who are hovering around the Ligue 1 relegation zone and have hired Vitor Matos out of Swansea to try to lift them. His is also a dry loan.

Mykhailo Mudryk is with Tottenham, where he has only played 16 minutes in total. He is now working his way back from what Roberto De Zerbi described as a ‘stupid’ ankle injury in training.

Spurs hold a lofty £75m option to buy the 25-year-old Ukrainian, who also did an ill-advised interview last week which was not approved by either Tottenham or Chelsea.

Sources indicate that axel Disasi, 28, is at bottom club Crystal Palace on a straightforward loan. If relegated, Disasi is unlikely to consider staying permanently, having made that clear when West Ham dropped down to the Championship last season.

Mykhailo Mudryk (right) is with Tottenham, where he has only played 16 minutes, thanks in part to an injury his boss Roberto De Zerbi described as 'stupid'.

Mamadou Sarr (left) is a rare case - a Chelsea loanee who is playing regularly for his new club, Real Sociedad.

In a recent development, benoit Badiashile, 25, is with Napoli, who have a £23.1m option to sign him permanently if they wish but have had a disappointing start in Serie A, lying down in eighth, 14 points behind league leaders Lazio. Badiashile has started three times in the league, and is currently injured.

Mamadou Sarr is with Real Sociedad, a loan which is also believed not to contain an option to buy, but the 21-year-old has been starting regularly for them in La Liga and the Europa League.

Other loans include Dastan Satpayev, the 18-year-old Kazakh who has been given a harsh welcome to English football with Championship strugglers Burnley (and is also injured), and Caleb Wiley, 21, also in the relegation zone with Preston.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards. The occasion was the world premiere of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" (released in the US and India as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone").

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

Sources indicate that daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour.".

The crowds showed just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

Today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

At first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

For years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

In a recent development, but in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an glitch Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

In an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

In a recent development, the controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

Others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

The "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

In a recent development, despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

Sources indicate that the eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been announced, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The new trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO says, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the new production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently mentioned she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

Meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

This article was originally written in German.
