📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of key saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Recent findings suggest that alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

According to recent reports, zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk.

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

It has been revealed that “I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager said. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

“I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

“We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

Recent findings suggest that it was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

According to recent reports, mcGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”.

Penalty MISSED! John McGinn hits the bar 💥 https://t.co/2kBYkYA2BY.

Nicolas Jackson was on hand to ease Villa’s nerves before the break, though. the Villa manager had mentioned before the game that the striker’s goalscoring capability meant he was capable of matching the likes of Harry Kane. His assessment was backed up by Jackson scoring the opening goal, after 40 minutes, which summed up the striker in one moment of pure power combined with agility.

Collecting Johan Manzambi’s superbly weighted pass, Jackson forced his way past two defenders before sliding in the goal that put Villa ahead.

Emery’s touchline celebrations said it all as the Senegal forward continues to flourish under the man who knew how to get the best out of him at Villarreal.

Nicolas Jackson scores his fifth league goal in five games! 🔥 https://t.co/W0xmFtW1Gt.

Suzuki has also flourished under Emery and he kept Villa in the game with some superb saves.

According to recent reports, when Antonee Robinson crossed for Gonzalo Garcia, his step over allowed Oscar Bobb in for what looked like his second goal in successive games. But Suzuki pulled off a stunning fingertip save. That had Villa supporters singing: “Zion Suzuki, the world’s No 1”.

It has been revealed that robinson put in another cross and Suzuki got a touch that was enough to make Garcia put his shot wide. Villa were living dangerously and the Japanese goalkeeper made another outstanding stop to keep out Iwobi’s header. But then it all went wrong for Suzuki when he fumbled Iwobi’s corner.

That allowed Fulham’s recent revival under manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, to continue – they now have seven points from their past three games.

Industry observers note that “We spoke at half-time about what we had to do,” Arbeloa remarked. “If you want to win a game you have to fight and I think we have to believe in our way, we’ve shown we can beat anyone in the way that we play but we have to be aggressive.

Industry observers note that “We created so many chances and at the end it’s one point in a difficult stadium. I’m so happy with the second half because of the way we played, this is the team that we want to be.”.

"This is the first time I've seen him that little bit confused" Rob Green analyses Zion Suzuki's error that lead to Fulham's equaliser 🔍 https://t.co/B3HCivNpwz.

"I don't think he gets the flowers he deserves" 💐 Jamie Redknapp is a fan of Calvin Bassey 🫡 https://t.co/R9uravAzRU.

“We started the game well. Fulham are a good side, not easy to win [against] but we came in front. We did well but in the second half we gave them more time on the ball. They have good players and they can make chances. We were unlucky with the goal but we tried to keep fighting. It is important not to lose these games.”.

On Zion Suzuki’s mistake for Fulham’s equaliser:.

“It is frustrating because we do not want to concede goals but it can happen to everyone. Zion is a great guy, great goalkeeper. He will learn from it. We will support him and go again.”.

Zion Suzuki had big gloves to fill this summer after the sale of Emiliano Martínez but already appears one of the Premier League signings of the summer.

Aston Villa’s new No 1 epitomises the vibrant energy of Unai Emery’s revamped squad and is a goalkeeper perfectly suited to the modern game.

The Japanese international is Villa’s own version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson, who revolutionised English football with a vast range of passing from his own penalty area.

Of all the daft statements to have come out of Aston Villa – and I am including Doug Ellis’s frequent claims that he invented the bicycle kick – it is hard to think of anything as absurd as suing a pundit for speaking the truth.

Jamie Carragher’s common-sense declaration that Villa manager Unai Emery might consider a move to Manchester United – because it is a bigger club – has apparently inflicted such a deep wound to the self-esteem of Nassef Sawiris, the chairman, that he has initiated a legal complaint.

Sawiris’s short statement, which he published on social media on Friday night, consisted of 37 ill-chosen words. It started by accusing Carragher of “unacceptable insults to the club and its fans”, then concluded with the vainglorious declaration that “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football”.

ASTON VILLA XI TO FACE FULHAM: Suzuki, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Goretzka, Alysson, Manzambi, McGinn, Jackson.

Subs: Bizot, Harwood-Bellis, Mings, Barkley, Buendia, Garnacho, Mbaye, Joao Gomes, Madjo.

FULHAM XI TO FACE ASTON VILLA: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, Bobb, King, Iwobi, Garcia.

Subs: Lecomte, Tete, Andersen, Palacios, Rodrigo Muniz, Cairney, Kevin, Larsson, Angel.

Referee: Sam Barrott (West Yorkshire).

Aston Villa manager, Unai Emery, is giving a full Premier League debut to Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka against Fulham this evening.

The 31-year-old joined Villa on a free transfer in the summer, but a knee injury prevented him from making an appearance off the bench until this month’s Champions League tie against Fenerbahce.

Asked what role Goretzka would have with Villa, Emery deadpanned: “The first one is to be available to play.”.

Sources indicate that emery had also made a cryptic remark about Nicolas Jackson and Johann Manzambi in his Friday press conference. The suggestion was that they had been merely rested for Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Bournemouth.

But the Spaniard said: “For different reasons, not only rest.”.

Whatever he meant is unclear, but both start for Villa tonight.

Fulham have won their last two league games – against Hull and Coventry.

Manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, has made one change with Sander Berge replacing Hugo Larsson in midfield.

Villa are aiming to win three successive league games for the first time in this calendar year. The omens are good as they’ve beaten Fulham in their last seven league meetings at Villa Park.

Your Villa starting XI tonight 🫡 #AVLFUL https://t.co/LCk7JJEKdD.

Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

In a recent development, “If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”.

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

Recent findings suggest that “It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa noted. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”.

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

#140332. Amorim: ‘Milan can defend better, were too soft in Europa League’

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (434 w)

Amorim: ‘Milan can defend better, were too soft in Europa League’

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (434 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Football-italia

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ruben Amorim insists that despite a very attacking Milan line-up against Olympiacos, they can ‘defend better’ than in previous ‘soft’ Europa League performances.
  • It kicks off at the Stadio Georgios Karaisakis in Piraeus at 17.45 GMT (18.45 CET).
  • You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game, Juventus-Omonia Nicosia and Borac-Atalanta on the Liveblog.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim insists that despite a very attacking Milan line-up against Olympiacos, they can ‘defend better’ than in previous ‘soft’ Europa League performances.

It kicks off at the Stadio Georgios Karaisakis in Piraeus at 17.45 GMT (18.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game, Juventus-Omonia Nicosia and Borac-Atalanta on the Liveblog.

The Rossoneri absolutely must get points in Greece this evening, because they lost three of their four Europa League games so far this season, winning 4-0 away to RB Salzburg.

They make the trip without Luka Modric, Francesco Camarda, Davide Bartesaghi, Strahinja Pavlovic, Samuel Chukwueze, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Pietro Terracciano.

It is an all-attack formation, with Diego Moreira, Alphadjo Cisse, Omari Hutchinson and Goncalo Ramos together.

It has been revealed that “In football, you need to defend and attack. Aside from the characteristics of the players, we need to attack with 11 and defend with 11,” Amorim told Sky Sport Italia.

Sources indicate that “The players know the positions that we want on the pitch, we are ready to play and must be more compact compared to the matches against Benfica and Ferencvaros. Even with these players, who are more attacking in their characteristics, we can defend better.”.

Milan have never won away to a Greek side in Europe, managing just four draws and two defeats, including a 3-1 loss to Olympiacos in December 2018.

It is notable that they have been unable to be consistent with two games in a week, so does Amorim see the right attitude today?

It has been revealed that “I think they understood, we watched the videos, we are improving as a team. We were a little soft against Ferencvaros because we were not compact, we need to really focus on the details, when the position makes all the difference two metres one way or another.

“We did it several times in Serie A, now we need to do it in the Europa League too.”.

Olympiacos can boast several former Serie A players, as Lorenzo Pirola was an Inter youth product, Remo Freuler spent time with Bologna and Atalanta, while Marcus Pedersen played for Torino.

In a recent development, “We need to be a good team, and to do that, we must be able to win in Serie A and in Europe. We have that responsibility, as we always say, the present is crucial, but we are in a long-term project. We need to know if we are ready and today is another important test for us to win,” concluded Amorim.

#140331. An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 29m • 📚 Deep Dive (5792 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

Latest Update: Everton Announces Partnership With Global Risk & Insurance Specialist WTW

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Evertonfc

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everton has confirmed a new multi-year partnership with WTW, a leading global advisory, broking and solutions organization, as the Club continues to expand its commercial portfolio into new categories.
  • Everton has confirmed a upcoming multi-year partnership with WTW, a leading global advisory, broking and solutions firm, as the Club continues to expand its commercial portfolio into new categories.
  • The agreement sees WTW become Everton’s ‘Official Insurance Partner’, bringing specialist expertise in insurance, risk management and analytics to support the Club’s operations and long-term ambitions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton has confirmed a new multi-year partnership with WTW, a leading global advisory, broking and solutions organization, as the Club continues to expand its commercial portfolio into new categories. The agreement sees WTW become Everton’s ‘Official Insurance Partner’, bringing specialist expertise in insurance, risk management and analytics to support the Club’s operations and long-term ambitions. Operating across more than 140 countries and markets, WTW becomes the latest internationally-recognised business to join Everton’s growing partnership portfolio, following recent agreements with NOCO, Nestlé and JYSK. Through the agreement, WTW will benefit from brand visibility at Hill Dickinson Stadium and across Everton’s digital and social media channels as well as commercial activation opportunities through access to the Club’s waterfront home for client hospitality, business events and engagement activities. The agreement allows for wider collaboration, including community initiatives, that will also be explored. As Everton’s exclusive partner in the insurance brokerage category, WTW will also provide tailored risk and insurance advice and solutions, drawing on its global insurance-market relationships and extensive experience across the sports and entertainment industry. Mark Rollings, Chief Partnerships Officer at Everton, noted: “We are delighted to welcome WTW as our Official Insurance Partner. “WTW is a highly respected global business with an outstanding reputation for expertise and innovation. This is a relationship that brings together two organisations with shared ambitions and a commitment to long-term success. “Alongside the international profile and opportunities Everton can offer WTW, the partnership will bring valuable specialist knowledge to the Club and create opportunities for collaboration beyond traditional sponsorship. “Welcoming another business of WTW’s calibre is a further demonstration of our commercial momentum and the growing appeal of Everton to leading international organisations.” WTW has an established presence across the global sports and entertainment sector, working with some the world’s best-known professional clubs, governing bodies, sporting events and venues to manage complex risks, strengthen resilience and support performance. Ian Tomlin, Global Sports and Entertainment Leader at WTW, said: “High-performing organisations, whether in sport or business, depend on resilience, specialist expertise and the confidence to make informed decisions. “Our partnership with Everton brings together the Club’s ambition and distinctive identity with WTW’s global insurance, risk and analytics expertise. “Together, we will help create greater resilience, improved risk management and performance, and lasting value on and off the pitch.”.

Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1338 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.
  • "The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he said, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.
  • A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.

"The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he said, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.

A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating. At the same time, states like Germany are slipping down the rankings for climate action, according to the annual Climate Change Performance Index published Wednesday by New Climate Institute and Germanwatch.

Nonetheless, Guterres mentioned the world has "the power to make sure the overshoot is a temporary breach.".

Negotiators from close to 200 countries are meeting in Turkey at the end of a year characterized by extreme heat waves and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a flood, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands more missing.

At this year's talks, national representatives are discussing climate solutions such as increasing the share of electricity in an effort to move away from fossil fuels.

On Thursday, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, one of the few heads of government from Europe's major economies attending the summit, noted that the world's dependence on fossil fuels was at the heart of both the climate crisis and energy security challenges.

"The shift to clean energy is the only route to energy security," he stated, endorsing the conference's focus on electrification which he said would lower energy bills, create jobs and protect people from the volatility of fossil fuel markets.

Burnham promised a "new era of British leadership over the next decade," announcing the UK would put climate resilience high on the agenda during its G20 presidency next year.

The US, the world's largest historical emitter of damaging greenhouse gases, is not attending the summit — for the second year in a row after US President Donald Trump withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement in 2025.

Other nations, including big polluters like Germany, France, Italy, Canada and Japan, also opted not to send their top leaders to the talks.

On Wednesday, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who is hosting COP31 together with Australia, which is leading negotiations, called on developed nations to take greater responsibility on climate finance.

In a recent development, financing disagreements center around who should pay for international climate action, whether funding should take the form of grants or loans and how to scale monetary support for developing nations. Many of these countries are among the most vulnerable to the climate crisis but have contributed very little to the emissions causing it.

It has been revealed that erdogan stated while previous conferences had resulted in different ideas around financing, they have yet to be turned into action. "We set out to make this an implementation COP," he told leaders.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen addressed remarks that developed nations are not contributing enough to climate finance, saying that the transition away from fossil fuels is in "our common interest.".

Recent findings suggest that "Europe is the world's largest provider of climate finance. Last year alone, we contributed more than €32 billion [about $35.5 billion] to support developing countries," she said, adding that Europe will continue to support partners worldwide in tackling climate change.

A recent Carbon Brief analysis found that public funding pledged under the Paris Agreement to help developing countries tackle climate change fell by more than 70% in 2026.

It has been revealed that most multi-year pledges from donor countries expired in 2025. Since then, the US has stepped back from international climate efforts, while several European countries have cut their aid budgets, reported Carbon Brief.

Hilda Heine, president of the Marshall Islands in the Pacific, which face an existential threat from rising sea levels, noted the response to overshoot "must be overwhelming" and promptly reversed otherwise "the world we know is over.".

"Every fraction of a degree of warming brings more catastrophe," said Heine, adding that more warming makes it more difficult to adapt to living on a hotter planet, brings greater loss and damage from worsening weather extremes and greater financial need.

She called on leaders to triple climate finance by 2035 and make it easier for Small Island Developing States to access the money.

"We are told there is no money, but their spending on war grows; the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death. Replenish the climate funds," Heine remarked.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese spoke of a "solemn responsibility to this and to future generations ​to act," adding that this is the critical decade.

Australia, the world's third-largest fossil fuel exporter, has vowed to promote the views of the "Pacific family" — small Pacific nations in the region such as Tuvalu or Fiji, where pre-COP meetings were held in October.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Albanese said it was crucial that climate cooperation delivered practical results — "unlocking investment in clean energy technologies, accelerating electrification, speeding up action for our oceans, unlocking climate finance for those who need it ​most.".

As reasons to speed up electrification von der Leyen pointed to wildfires in Europe and floods in Nepal, as well as droughts stretching from Central America to Sudan, and to the disruption to energy supplies linked to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

"The world is witnessing the cost of continuing with the status quo for our climate and our energy security," she mentioned, adding that the European Union would double down on efforts to become climate neutral.

"Three-quarters ​of humanity live in countries that import fossil fuels, hostage to price shocks they did ​not create and cannot ‌control," UN Secretary-General Guterres noted, adding that recent conflicts have made clear a shift to renewable energy would help improve energy security and the cost-of-living crisis.

Recent findings suggest that von der Leyen also expressed support for COP31's 35-by-35 electrification pledge. The pledge aims to increase electricity's share of final global energy use to 35% by 2035, with von der Leyen saying Europe would be the first "electro-powered" continent.

Heine of the Marshall Islands noted electrification must must be strictly tied to renewable energy generation rather than fossil fuels, warning that continued oil, coal and gas extraction was a threat to her country's survival.

Recent findings suggest that iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country wanted compensation for environmental damage caused by US and Israeli strikes, including oil leaks from attacks on tankers. The strikes began in February.

Iran, which is a major fossil fuel producer and has pushed back against strict language on phasing out oil and gas at previous COPs alongside other petrostates, has also struck tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Pezeshkian linked the issue to climate finance and said his country expected "responsibility in times of war, to document and assess the environmental damages caused by military aggressions and to develop compensation mechanisms.".

Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who hosted last year's COP in the Amazonian city of Belem, said the momentum for climate action had dropped off at the start of the year, partly due to the Iran war.

"We started talking more about weapons and tariffs than the survival ‌of future generations," he said.

Recent findings suggest that he also warned that "climate agreements are the favorite targets of reactionary forces at COPs," and urged leaders to work together. Lula promised to protect the Amazon rainforest. "Brazil is back to defend the continuity of a healthy planet," he said.

This article was last updated on November 12 to reflect incoming statements from world leaders.

Oliver Glasner has criticised Nottingham Forest players that cannot speak English after being in the country for several years, as he called for higher standards at the club.

Forest are currently outside the Premier League relegation zone on goal difference after 11 matches, having won just twice in the top flight since Glasner's arrival in the summer.

Speaking ahead of their Friday night clash against Chelsea, Glasner highlighted the failure of some of his squad to learn English to illustrate how standards needed to rise at the club.

It has been revealed that 'Stability in a manufacturer is having standards,' Glasner said. 'Everybody who joins commits to the standards. I think, very honestly, the standards were not high enough.

Recent findings suggest that 'We have players who are here for four years, can't speak English. If you go to Italy, after three months, every player gives his interview in the Italian language.

It has been revealed that 'For me, if I want to manage in England, I have to speak English. If I want to manage in Italy, I have to speak Italian.

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner has criticised stars for failing to speak English years after joining the club.

Glasner highlighted the issue as an example as he insisted standards need to rise at the club.

'Otherwise, Oliver Glasner, if you want to speak in your dialect, stay at home in Austria, everybody understands you, but nowhere else.'.

Football clubs regularly enlist the services of language experts in an effort to help foreign stars to settle and communicate with their team-mates.

West Brom and Wolves have worked with Language Partners for around 20 years, with the firm providing tailored classes to players and coaches, offering specific skills required for their role at the clubs.

Another company, Communicate Well, has worked with Premier League clubs since 1999, with lessons taking place at training grounds, players’ homes and ‘out and about’ to provide real-life tasks in English.

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez previously revealed Arsenal had included a £20,000 bonus in his first contract with the club, which would be paid when he passed the English proficiency test.

Martinez, who signed for Arsenal in the summer of 2010 from Argentine side Independiente, had reportedly passed the test before Christmas.

English stars moving abroad have received praise in recent years for their efforts to learn the native language, with Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Trent Alexander-Arnold having all made efforts to become fluent in Spanish.

Alexander-Arnold revealed he had worked with a Spanish tutor for five months prior to joining Real Madrid. The tutor revealed he had started ‘from zero’ but worked every day to be able to speak Spanish at his unveiling at the club.

According to recent reports, after speaking Spanish at his Barcelona unveiling, Gordon explained he had initially begun learning the language at Everton when working under Rafael Benitez. He later spoke Spanish with a physio at Newcastle as he targeted a move to Barcelona, while the winger also underwent six formal lessons.

Joao Gomes is among Wolves' foreign imports to have worked with a specialist language firm to help them settle at the club.

Arsenal put a bonus in Emiliano Martinez's contract to encourage him to learn English.

Trent Alexander-Arnold worked with a Spanish tutor for five months before his move to Real Madrid.

Daily Mail Sport reported last month that Glasner had not been happy with some of his players' attitudes and their response to his work since joining the club from Crystal Palace in the summer.

Glasner had explosively hit out at his players after their 2-0 defeat at Brentford at the end of October, with the Austrian having warned players either had to buy into his methods to see a turnaround in form or they would have a sixth manager since the start of last season.

The 52-year-old's warning appeared to have been met with a positive response as Forest earned a stunning 3-1 victory over Man City before the international break, but they returned with a 2-0 loss at Bournemouth last weekend.

Glasner had maintained that his squad will have to work hard and show commitment both on and off the pitch to improve.

'We always try to support the players to get the best version of themselves that they can be. But at the end, the players that have to do it, they have to buy in, they have to listen and work hard on the pitch,' Glasner noted.

'There is no other opportunity to improve, it would be easy laying on the sofa and doing nothing and you become a better football player or suddenly speak a language all of a sudden.

It has been revealed that 'It just doesn't work. It is all about how hard you work and how committed you are.

Glasner has insisted his squad need to work hard and show commitment to improve.

'I believe none of our players have reached his personal ceilings so far, there is always bits to improve – physically, mentally, technically, tactically – there is always space to improve.

'The most important thing is that players want to improve, then it can happen.'.

Glasner met with Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis in London earlier this week, where intends for the January transfer window were discussed.

Forest are expected to target adding around five players to their squad in the window as they bid to turn around their fortunes.

'He was asking "what do you need, what do you want here to improve in the squad, the staff and the environment",' Glasner said.

'He wants the best for Nottingham Forest, he wants the best for everyone here.

Sources indicate that 'We need to improve in the squad, in the staff, in the environment and this is our discussion. It was a fantastic meeting and it was worth spending six hours travelling.'.

Forest face a Chelsea side on Friday that have lost three of their last four league matches.

Glasner’s side will then begin December with matches against Hull, Brighton and Sunderland as they bid to climb the table.

  • Football's governing body confirmed that a hacking group 'impersonated staff' to gain access to their system before taking the sensitive files.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:12 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 08:10 EST, 26 November 2026.

Personal information, immigration documents and financial records have been stolen from FIFA in a cyberattack.

Football's governing body confirmed that a hacking group 'impersonated staff' to gain access to their system before taking the sensitive files.

In total, more than 12 gigabytes of data has been stolen and a group called Handsome Boy Hacking Club (HBHC) shared a screenshot of FIFA documents on X last week, claiming credit for the theft and finding access through FIFA’s Microsoft app portal.

They are understood to have then published the stolen files on a forum on the dark web, writing 'more leaks soon'.

A FIFA spokesperson mentioned: 'FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyber-attack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information.

'FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement.

FIFA were hacked and had sensitive documents stolen - pictured, FIFA president Gianni Infantino.

Handsome Boy Hacking Club took credit for the hack and shared this screenshot on X.

'FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data.

'Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.'.

According to the Athletic, immigration, financial and personal documents were stolen by the hackers impersonating staff but did not include the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a strategy to effectively sell off the World Cup that collapsed and piled pressure on president Gianni Infantino.

The FFE plan first became public knowledge in July. Infantino sought to create a company to manage the commercial interests of FIFA’s competitions, including the World Cup, but wanted a minority stake to be made available to private investors.

The lead investor was set to be Thrive, a company founded by President Trump’s son-in-law’s brother, Josh Kushner, but the plan was abandoned on August 1 after three continental confederations rejected it.

It remains to be seen whether files relating to Infantino himself were taken by the hackers.

The 56-year-old is currently running for reelection against Kohzo Tashima of Japan and France football federation president Philippe Diallo.

He remains the strong favorite to win FIFA's election is held on March 18 and has already served three terms.

FIFA are the latest football-related body to have fallen victim to cyber crime, with LaLiga targeted earlier this month.

Spanish police are still investigating but LaLiga confirmed their security teams identified the source and stopped the hacker from stealing more data.

#140316. Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1042 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.
  • For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.
  • In late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.

For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.

In late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank. It remains unclear whether this complaint will lead to an independent investigation.

The AIIB, which finances major infrastructure projects across Asia, has a mechanism in place to deal with such complaints.

Individuals who suffer adverse effects from the bank-financed projects may, under certain conditions, file a complaint with the institution.

However, access to this process — known as the Project Complaints Mechanism (PPM) — remains controversial.

According to a report by The Diplomat, a magazine that covers political and economic developments in Asia, none of the 45 complaints listed on the AIIB's website had been deemed admissible as of mid-September.

The bank acknowledged that "no cases have passed the PPM's eligibility assessment," but it stressed that this is "only part of the story.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The AIIB emphasized that not every glitch needs to be resolved through this mechanism.

The PPM is "only one part of AIIB's grievance redress ecosystem," the Beijing-based bank stated in response to a query from DW.

Those affected should first attempt to resolve concerns directly with the project team at the local level, it said.

According to the bank, "twelve complaints were in fact resolved at the project level — as a direct result of AIIB's follow-up and intervention — and one was resolved through domestic courts.".

But critics see this as a major weakness.

"The mechanism must be easily accessible," mentioned Arntraud Hartmann, a development economist at the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS Europe) in Bologna, Italy.

She argued that people affected by the projects, for instance, are required to document potential violations of environmental and social standards from the start. "How is the affected party supposed to know which standards might have been violated?" she questioned.

In a recent development, the AIIB disputes this claim. "In terms of accessibility, we have made the submission form simpler and translated it into 12 languages," it said, adding that complaints can be submitted online, by phone, or by email.

Urgewald, a German environmental NGO, cites another problem with AIIB-financed projects. For many of them, information on environmental impacts and resettlements is either missing or published late, it noted.

For 2024, the NGO found that 11 of the 16 projects it examined lacked complete environmental and social impact assessments. In many cases, information on the potential number of displaced residents was also missing, it added.

Sources indicate that "The information published on the bank's website is often insufficient and inconsistent. Particularly important documents, such as environmental impact assessments or resettlement plans, vary widely or are missing entirely," mentioned Nora Sausmikat, a China expert at Urgewald.

The lack of information makes it difficult for those affected to respond promptly and report violations early on, she underscored, adding that the situation is particularly difficult for people without formal land titles.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Christoph Steinert, a political scientist at the University of Konstanz, said the mere existence of such grievance redressal mechanisms "is not enough.".

Particularly vulnerable groups often know little about their rights, he remarked, adding that information should be available in local languages and targeted outreach directed at affected communities.

It has been revealed that criticism of the AIIB's procedures is not latest. A 2023 report by international aid organizations, including Recourse, Accountability Counsel, and Inclusive Development International, revealed that the AIIB's grievance mechanism had failed to accept a single complaint since its 2019 inception.

The study highlighted that 101 of the 219 AIIB-financed projects, or 46% of the total projects at the time, were ineligible for review due to co-financing exemptions.

The AIIB typically provides funding without leading projects, a standard practice in development finance. When complaints arise, it directs complainants to the lead lender. As a result, nine of the 45 complaints fell outside its jurisdiction.

For Sausmikat, this is part of the problem. "The AIIB, however, decided against revising this requirement and established a mechanism that is very difficult to access," she noted.

In a recent development, as of January 1, 2026, following two years of external consultations, the AIIB reformed its complaints mechanism. Under certain conditions, complaints can now be filed even while legal proceedings are ongoing.

Industry observers note that but Sausmikat stressed that the changes are insufficient. Of the eight key recommendations made by an independent expert, only three were adopted, she underlined. "The revision did not remove the actual obstacles.".

The AIIB stated that the reforms are intended to make the mechanism "more accessible and responsive.".

The upcoming rules have been in effect for only 10 months, and their implementation is being closely monitored, the bank stated.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Steinert said fear of reprisals poses another fundamental challenge to such procedures.

Documented cases from Latin America, for instance, show that complainants have faced administrative or legal problems, and in some cases even violence.

Recent findings suggest that such risks could deter others from filing complaints, Steinert remarked. However, his research does not specifically address AIIB projects.

The bank said that it "does not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises concerns.".

"Requestors may ask for confidentiality, and the revised PPM policy strengthens protection against reprisals," it added.

Sausmikat noted Germany — as a co-founder and the fourth-largest shareholder of the AIIB — could also play a role, working with other member states to push for changes.

Industry observers note that hartmann also stressed that the bank's shareholders bear responsibility and urged the AIIB's Board of Directors to amend the rules governing the grievance mechanism. "We need a policy based on good-practice standards.".

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, this Christmas, Everton in the Community is calling on supporters to help tackle loneliness and bring the true Christmas Spirit of the Blues to those who need it most. Loneliness can affect anyone, at any time of the year. It could be an older person facing another Christmas without their loved ones, a young person struggling to find where they belong, a parent finding it difficult to cope or someone surrounded by people but still feeling alone. That's why the official charitable arm of Everton Football Club is launching Christmas Spirit of the Blues, a campaign dedicated to raising awareness of loneliness in all its forms and ensuring everyone knows there is somewhere they can turn. Dedicated to breaking down barriers and supporting its local community since 1988, Everton in the Community delivers more than 50 inclusive, free programmes, each designed to tackle different societal challenges. From supporting young people back into education and giving latest fathers access to vital support networks, to helping military veterans navigate life after the forces, each programme shares the same ambition - to improve confidence, provide a sense of belonging and remind people just how important they are. To launch the campaign, Everton in the Community brought together participants, staff, supporters and players past and present at Hill Dickinson Stadium for a special performance of the iconic Liverpool Express hit, Spirit of the Blues. Liverpool-based brass band Allerton Brass performed a slowed-down version of the track, creating a poignant moment of togetherness and highlighting the power of music to bring people together. Throughout the build-up to Christmas, the campaign will shine a light on the experiences of people who have faced loneliness and explore how finding support, friendship and a sense of belonging has made a difference to their lives. Among those sharing their stories is Gina, who has found cherished friendships through Everton in the Community's Stand Together programme following the loss of her husband, and a young man whose experience of loneliness brought him to the brink of suicide. The campaign will also hear from father-of-two Sean, who reached out to Everton in the Community in the middle of the night after his wife tragically died just 12 hours after giving birth to their second son. “My newborn baby and his two-year-old brother were asleep, and I found myself feeling completely alone, drowning in grief and crying uncontrollably. “It was a hail Mary. I just needed to reach out to someone and, as an Evertonian, I knew about Everton in the Community – but I didn't expect the level of help I did get. It was a lifesaver.”  At a time when his world had been turned upside down, Sean indicates reaching out gave him someone to turn to when he felt he had nowhere else to go, and marked the first step towards navigating life without his wife. Dan Halliday, Head of Fundraising at Everton in the Community, said: “For thousands of people across the Liverpool City Region and beyond, loneliness, social isolation and grief can feel even heavier at Christmas. “The pressure to feel happy or the absence of familiar handwriting on a Christmas card can be painful reminders of what's missing. “This Christmas, a donation to Everton in the Community could help someone feel seen, supported and part of something bigger. Together, we can make sure nobody has to face loneliness alone.”  To donate to Everton in the Community and join our mission to end loneliness together, visit (insert link). For more information about accessing support, visit https://www.evertoninthecommunity.org/projects/minds/accessing-mental-health-support/.

This Christmas, Everton in the Community is calling on supporters to help tackle loneliness and bring the true Christmas Spirit of the Blues to those who need it most.

Recent findings suggest that loneliness can affect anyone, at any time of the year. It could be an older person facing another Christmas without their loved ones, a young person struggling to find where they belong, a parent finding it difficult to cope or someone surrounded by people but still feeling alone.

That's why the official charitable arm of Everton Football Club is launching Christmas Spirit of the Blues, a campaign dedicated to raising awareness of loneliness in all its forms and ensuring everyone knows there is somewhere they can turn.

Dedicated to breaking down barriers and supporting its local community since 1988, Everton in the Community delivers more than 50 inclusive, free programmes, each designed to tackle different societal challenges.

From supporting young people back into education and giving newly introduced fathers access to vital support networks, to helping military veterans navigate life after the forces, each programme shares the same ambition - to improve confidence, provide a sense of belonging and remind people just how notable they are.

To launch the campaign, Everton in the Community brought together participants, staff, supporters and players past and present at Hill Dickinson Stadium for a special performance of the iconic Liverpool Express hit, Spirit of the Blues.

Liverpool-based brass band Allerton Brass performed a slowed-down version of the track, creating a poignant moment of togetherness and highlighting the power of music to bring people together.

Throughout the build-up to Christmas, the campaign will shine a light on the experiences of people who have faced loneliness and explore how finding support, friendship and a sense of belonging has made a difference to their lives.

Among those sharing their stories is Gina, who has found cherished friendships through Everton in the Community's Stand Together programme following the loss of her husband, and a young man whose experience of loneliness brought him to the brink of suicide.

The campaign will also hear from father-of-two Sean, who reached out to Everton in the Community in the middle of the night after his wife tragically died just 12 hours after giving birth to their second son.

“My newborn baby and his two-year-old brother were asleep, and I found myself feeling completely alone, drowning in grief and crying uncontrollably.

“It was a hail Mary. I just needed to reach out to someone and, as an Evertonian, I knew about Everton in the Community – but I didn't expect the level of help I did get. It was a lifesaver.”.

At a time when his world had been turned upside down, Sean states reaching out gave him someone to turn to when he felt he had nowhere else to go, and marked the first step towards navigating life without his wife.

Dan Halliday, Head of Fundraising at Everton in the Community, mentioned: “For thousands of people across the Liverpool City Region and beyond, loneliness, social isolation and grief can feel even heavier at Christmas.

“The pressure to feel happy or the absence of familiar handwriting on a Christmas card can be painful reminders of what's missing.

Recent findings suggest that “This Christmas, a donation to Everton in the Community could help someone feel seen, supported and part of something bigger. Together, we can make sure nobody has to face loneliness alone.”.

To donate to Everton in the Community and join our mission to end loneliness together, visit (insert link).

For more information about accessing support, visit https://www.evertoninthecommunity.org/projects/minds/accessing-mental-health-support/.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

It has been revealed that A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

Sources indicate that few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

“The mission was something we didn’t complete in 14 years,” Mikel Arteta stated, having famously – in an Amazon documentary series – played You’ll Never Walk Alone to his players as they walked out to train to try and overcome a perceived mental block.

Recent findings suggest that “There are reasons for that. Some of it psychological, some of it moments we did not nail on the pitch,” the Arsenal manager added of the winless run.

Recent findings suggest that the result means that the north Londoners have already now won away at Villa Park, the Stadium of Light, the City Ground and Anfield. Stadiums where they dropped points last season. And that feels ominous.

In a recent development, A win would maybe have thrust Liverpool into the title race. Instead, under Andoni Iraola, and with an evolving young team – with promising 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni handed his league debut – they are already nine points behind after just nine matches.

It is also clear, however, that they could have prevented this defeat having somehow been denied a first-half penalty after Alexander Isak’s shirt was blatantly pulled by Jurrien Timber as the striker tried to head home a cross.

Sources indicate that referee Andy Madley may have missed it, but what was the excuse of Stuart Attwell, the VAR? It was a stunningly poor decision – another bad day for Pro Ref and the use of technology.

It might be argued that Timber did not pull hard enough to prevent Isak from reaching the ball. But the defender grabbed the shirt and continued to hold it for a long time. It had to be a penalty. Little wonder Iraola said Isak should dive next time. Who can blame him?

What is also clear and obvious is that, once again, Arsenal’s resilience, defensive determination and appetite for toughing it out will be their greatest weapons. They are certainly, under Arteta, not here to win friends – just to win matches and trophies.

“That defensive line, that togetherness we have is undefeated. It’s something I have never seen before,” Declan Rice, who was also a stand-out performer and delivered a fine assist for the winner, said.

According to recent reports, arsenal’s version of the Yellow Wall was, indeed, hugely impressive – it is now six clean sheets from their nine league games and, despite all their pressure, Liverpool did not have a shot on target. That has never happened in the Premier League since such statistics started to be compiled in 2003 (422 games ago).

“That’s incredible. It did not feel like it on the pitch. Again, it’s the commitment of every single player,” Arteta said. And that was indisputable.

In a recent development, even the expected second-half momentum, the expected surge of attack after attack as Liverpool faced the Kop, crashed on Arsenal’s back line. The visitors were so well-drilled that they stifled space – they refused to crumble.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal put their bodies on the line with blocks and tackles and a bit of time-wasting. There were dark arts, especially from both centre-halves with Gabriel going unpunished after claiming he was struck in the face by Isak early on – VAR anyone? – and the otherwise outstanding Ezri Konsa throwing himself to the ground after minimal contact from the Liverpool centre-forward.

Recent findings suggest that in fairness there was also a bit of that from an increasingly frustrated Liverpool with Alexis Mac Allister going down after touching heads with Noni Madueke, having already tried to provoke Martin Odegaard with a hand to the head when the Arsenal captain was on the turf. That was not good from Mac Allister either.

And the only goal? Again, more frustration for Liverpool. It was well-constructed from Arsenal, but only after Alisson Becker’s loose goal kick, aimed towards Jérémy Jacquet, who was slow to react, was intercepted by Odegaard with Bruno Guimarães poking the ball to the right, where it was collected by Madueke.

According to recent reports, there was an overlap by Rice and his low centre was precise and dangerous across the face of the six-yard area, with Virgil van Dijk unsure what to do. It ran beyond the far post where Kai Havertz side-footed home.

"Absolutely brilliant from Arsenal." Kai Havertz gives Arsenal an early lead at Anfield! ⚡️ https://t.co/eeyhRcLlel.

After that? Liverpool swarmed over Arsenal, particularly in the first-half with Florian Wirtz’s free-kick cannoning back off the crossbar and Mac Allister somehow heading over. He was six yards out and unmarked, it was a glorious chance.

That was the hosts’ last tangible opportunity to score. As well as Arsenal defended, it was not a good afternoon for Liverpool’s forwards, Bradley Barcola in particular, although it was interesting to see Arsenal double-up on Rio Ngumoha when he came on. Arteta reacted by bringing on a second left-back, in Piero Hincapié.

Pride? No disappointment. Disappointment. We played at home. We had some opportunities. Obviously we tried everything. We could have done better in the last 15 minutes to get balls in the box but it wasn’t enough. That’s why it’s a disappointment.

After we conceded we started to play much better. We created the big chance for Alexis which could have changed the game. It didn’t happen. We kept pushing and pushing.

I think there was also a clear penalty. I have seen it back. I’ve seen it being given on other occasions. [Should Alex have made more of it. Maybe the VAR doesn’t notice it…] The VAR doesn’t notice it? We have 50 cameras, even more. Why do you have to complain more if they have 50 cameras. They spotted it because everyone’s seen it. It wasn’t given, we lose the game. Congratulations to Arsenal.

When someone new comes in the building it just takes a bit if time. Our fans can see there is so much improvement and we work out socks off. What we do need as well is results.

In a recent development, havertz: “It means a lot to the whole football club. It is notable. It’s what they deserve [the fans]. We all know what this stadium is about. We knew it was coming but we all stuck together, defended together. Ninety per cent of the goal belongs to that man [Rice].”.

Rice: “That’s the Anfield way. That is what Liverpool do. This stadium creates waves and waves of attacks. Relentless. That defensive line, that togetherness we have is undefeated. It’s something I’ve never seen before. The manager had an honest conversation with me and said I could do even more for this club [in terms of assists and goals]. It’s always tiring coming here. First win in 14 years and my first win here too. It’s demanding. An amazing result. I have learnt that you can only take the table seriously in February and March and all you can do until then is win as many as you can.”.

Just eight universities dominate Nobel and other top economics prizes

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1105 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers from Harvard and seven other US universities including MIT, Princeton and Yale, dominate economics prizes.Credit: Jade Gao/AFP via Getty.
  • Major prizes in economics, including the Nobel are being awarded to researchers affiliated to an increasingly concentrated set of US universities, according to a working paper published last month1.
  • Eight institutions dominate the world's top economics prizes, led Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers from Harvard and seven other US universities including MIT, Princeton and Yale, dominate economics prizes.Credit: Jade Gao/AFP via Getty.

Major prizes in economics, including the Nobel are being awarded to researchers affiliated to an increasingly concentrated set of US universities, according to a working paper published last month1.

Eight institutions dominate the world's top economics prizes, led Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Industry observers note that this contrasts with prizes awarded in disciplines in the natural sciences, engineering and social sciences outside economics. These have become less concentrated among certain instituions over the past 70 years, according to the working paper, which has not yet been peer reviewed.

Sources indicate that “The whole world now does science,” says Richard Freeman, an economist at Harvard University and an author on the paper, which is an update to an article presented at a National Bureau of Economic Research Summer Institute workshop in a 20242. “Our initial thought was that as the science spreads out, so too should all the prizes.” And that was the case — except in economics where “it went the other direction”.

Economist John Hassler, who is based at Stockholm University and chairs the prize-awarding committee for the Economics Prize in Memory of Alfred Nobel, states that the overall finding of concentration among a small group of US universities is not a complete surprise.

“The trend is truly eye-opening and adds another dimension to the understanding of inequality within the economics profession,” adds Ashwini Deshpande, an economist at Ashoka University in Sonipat, India. “The low levels of gender, ethnic and geographic diversity within authors of top journal papers and prizes is well known and a matter of concern.”.

Freeman and his colleagues examined 171 different awards and focused their analyses on those given between 1960 and 2022, including Nobel prizes (except for literature and peace), the Fields Medal for mathematics and the Breakthrough science prizes established in 2012 by the founders of technology companies among others.

The authors of the working paper analysed the academic affiliations of the 5,859 prizewinners, working out the number of years they were linked to a specific institution. They call this metric ‘affiliation years’.

Of the 18 scientific fields of the prizewinners, 17 had a greater variety of universities represented among recipients over the time period. Economics was the outlier.

Among winners of the economics Nobel prize, seven out of 148 institutions made up 50% of affiliation years. It means that, of all the years that economics Nobel prizewinners dedicated to their discipline in academia, half of them were spent in the seven institutions.

For chemistry Nobels, 23 institutions out of 216 accounted for half of affiliation years. Twenty-six out of 243 institutions accounted for 50% of affiliation years for the physiology or medicine Nobel, and 17 out of 200 for the physics prize.

Sources indicate that when the authors assessed all the main economics prizes between 1960 and 2022 (not only the Nobel), they found that researchers from eight out of 249 institutions represented 50% of affiliation years. In addition to Harvard, the eight are: the University of Chicago in Illinois; Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in Cambridge; Stanford University in California; Princeton University in New Jersey; Yale University in New Haven, Connecticut; the University of California, Berkeley; and Columbia University in New York.

By contrast, for assessed prizes in the natural sciences, 37 institutions out of 1,318 account for 50% of affiliation-years as of 2022; for engineering prizes it is 27 out of 783; and for social sciences prizes (minus economics), it is 23 out of 744. Unlike in economics, the trend for these fields is towards less concentration (see ‘Spot the outlier’).

Recent findings suggest that the authors propose some possible explanations. One of these relates to another finding of the paper: “The institutions producing most of the field’s recognized work also establish the toolkit that the rest of the fields adopts,” the paper’s authors say. “Work using an unfamiliar approach is hard to place or recognize, and findings that disagree with the main tenets of the field are rejected rather than studied as special cases that may yield fresh knowledge.”.

Another factor, they report is that in economics, 55 per cent of Nobel laureates received the prize for a broad body of work. This contrasts somewhat with medicine and the other sciences. Some 50 per cent of prize winners in chemistry, 59 per cent in physics and 70 per cent in medicine were awarded for testable findings.

Hanzhang Zhou, a co-author on the paper and an economics doctoral candidate at MIT, says: “When you’re giving the prize for somebody’s lifetime agenda, the institution that they’re associated with is usually one of the factors that you do take into account,” she explains.

Hassler told Nature that the economics prize is not intended to be a lifetime achievement award and follows the rules governing the other prize categories. He says it is a prize for a well-defined contribution or breakthrough, should also lead to further research in the field and that the finding must also have relevance to society at large.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03333-3.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juventus start Francisco Conceicao, Jeremie Boga and Jeff Ekhator in a fresh 3-4-2-1 formation with Neto in goal as they host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League.

It kicks off at the Allianz Juventus Stadium in Turin at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game, Olympiacos-Milan and Borac-Atalanta on the Liveblog.

The Bianconeri have done well in the Europa League so far this season, winning every fixture except their 2-2 draw with Stade Rennais.

This is a must-win match for their hopes of going through directly to the Round of 16 as one of the top eight teams, but Luciano Spalletti must also rotate the squad.

He is still missing Pierre Kalulu, Nico Gonzalez, Kerim Alajbegovic, Khephren Thuram, Manuel Locatelli, Arek Milik and Kamil Grabara, while Edon Zhegrova and Daniele Rugani are not on the UEFA list.

The good news is Juve have Francisco Conceicao back in the starting XI for his first appearance since the shoulder injury on October 18.

He is part of a 3-4-2-1 formation with Ekhator as centre-forward and Boga in the trident.

Neto also gets his first start in goal for Juventus, albeit in his second spell at the club, having last featured in this jersey in May 2017.

Omonia Nicosia sit fourth in their domestic league, and had originally been in the Champions League preliminary rounds, dropping into the Europa League.

They started this season strong, beating Celta Vigo and Celje, but then lost 4-1 at home to Benfica and 3-1 away to NEC Nijmegen.

They have Fotis Kitsos and Mihlali Mayambela injured, while Carel Eiting, Moses Odubajo, David Akintola and Giorgos Viktoros are cup-tied.

Lois Diony is by a long way their top scorer this season with 11 goals in 20 competitive appearances, but only one in the Europa League.

Juventus: Neto; Gatti, Lucumi, Kelly; Cabal, Douglas Luiz, Sarr, Cambiaso; Conceicao, Boga; Ekhator.

Omonia Nicosia: Kaminski; Duverne, Coulibaly, Satka, Nego; Andreou, Maric; Tanase, Tankovic, Montnor; Kakoullis.
